units.label: The rock cycle overview (text)
units.content_summary: Rocks are classified into three types based on how they form: igneous (cooled magma/lava), sedimentary (compressed sediment layers), metamorphic (transformed by heat and pressure). The rock cycle describes how one type can become another.

units.label: Rock cycle diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Circular diagram showing igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks connected by arrows labeled with processes: melting, cooling, compaction, heat/pressure, weathering.

units.label: Sample rock photos (image)
units.content_summary: Three photos side by side: granite (igneous, speckled), sandstone (sedimentary, layered), and gneiss (metamorphic, banded).

units.label: Identification guide (text)
units.content_summary: Key visual clues: igneous rocks often have crystals or glassy texture; sedimentary rocks show visible layers or grains; metamorphic rocks show banding or foliation from pressure.

units.label: Practice: classify these rocks (text)
units.content_summary: Four rock descriptions given (layered with visible sand grains, glassy black rock, banded grey/white rock, rock with large mineral crystals). Classify each as igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.
